description: `ungroup` has a returning guard `if (!rows || !rows.length) return []`. Its empty case is reached only through `group()`, whose rest parameter is always an array, so no test passes a nullish `rows`. `!rows` is evaluated on every call and is never true. Istanbul records binary-expr [3, 3] and 100% branches, and deleting `!rows ||` keeps every test green: the radashi `unzip` case from BL-039. KNOWN MISS: `untested-condition-operand` stays silent. Its never-evaluated signal needs a zero count, and its never-decisive signal only handles guards that throw. BL-040 would prove this survivor from the equal counts; when it lands, move the pattern to expectedBugPatterns.
